result.topic_en: Treatment of the second case m = 2 of the heat-conduction prize problem: the equation splits into Δu = 0 and Λu = ∂u/∂t, normal forms for Δ are given, ΔΛu = 0 is derived, and two sub-cases (α) ΔΛ = θΔ and (β) are distinguished, with (α) investigated for Δ = ∂_α∂_β + e∂_α + f∂_β.
result.transcription:
Pariser Aufgabe. 5.

Casus secundus $m=2$.

Quem casum quum infra visuri simus in corporibus homogeneis occurrere non posse, hic brevioribus esse nobis licet. Si (aequatio (1) in duas aequationes a $y$ independentes discinditur, ope alterius $\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$ ex altera ejici potest) Brevitatis causa haec ita exhibeatur
$(1)\ \Delta u = 0$
illa
$(2)\ \Lambda u = \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$
denotantibus $\Delta$ et $\Lambda$ expressiones characteristicas ex $\partial_\alpha$ et $\partial_\beta$ conflatas. Aequationem priorem facile perspicitur mutatis variabilibus independentibus ita transformari posse, ut sit $\Delta$
vel [-$\Delta$-] $= \partial_\alpha\partial_\beta + e\partial_\alpha + f\partial_\beta$
vel $= \partial_\alpha^2 + e\partial_\alpha + f\partial_\beta$
vel $= \partial_\alpha$
valoribus $e=0$, $f=0$ non exclusis.
Quum sit
$0 = \partial_t\Delta u = \Delta\partial_t u = \Delta\Lambda u$
ex his duabus aequationibus sequitur
$(3)\ \Delta\Lambda u = 0$
Iam duo distinguendi sunt casus, prout haec aequatio (3) vel ex aequatione (1) fluat ($\alpha$) sive sit
$\Delta\Lambda = \theta\Delta$
denotante $\theta$ novam expressionem characteristicam vel non fluat ($\beta$) novamque aequationem a $\Delta u = 0$ independentem sistat.
(Tum $\Delta\Lambda u$ ope aequationis $\Delta u = 0$ ad expressionem reduci potest, quae solas derivationes secundum alteram utram variabilem contineat et coefficientes omnes cifrae aequales habere debeat.)
Casum priorem ($\alpha$) ut saltem pro una forma ipsius $\Delta$ perscrutemur, supponamus
$\Delta = \partial_\alpha\partial_\beta + e\partial_\alpha + f\partial_\beta$.
Tum ope aequationis $\Delta u = 0$ ex $\Delta\Lambda u = 0$ omnes derivationes secundum ambas variabiles ejici possunt, quo facto necesse est coefficientes reliquarum evanescant. Ponamus, quum terminus $\partial_\alpha\partial_\beta$ ope aequationis $\Delta u$ ejici possit,
$\Lambda = a\partial_\alpha^2 + b\partial_\beta^2 + c\partial_\alpha + d\partial_\beta$
